mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals economic weakness, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over a quarter signals a supply-side contraction, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declined by more than 2% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over a quarter signals an economic contraction, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE).
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declined by more than 1% in a quarter, especially if UNRATE also increased.
